description: Pack an item into a container — a case, cart or box that is itself an inventory item (e.g. put the voltmeter into the experiment case). While packed, the item's location and holder FOLLOW the container: moving or lending the whole kit is ONE assign_item call on the container, and item reads show the followed position as effectiveLocation/effectiveHolder. A container can have named compartments (a vehicle's «Fahrerhaus», «GR1»…«GR7» — get_item on the container lists them as `compartments`): pass `compartment` (its name, case-insensitive, or its id) to put the item there; an unknown name is refused with `unknownCompartment` and the container's `validNames`. Pass `compartment: null` to put it directly in the container, outside any compartment (also to take it out of its compartment within the same container). Without `compartment`, re-packing into the same container keeps the item's compartment, and packing into another container puts it directly in it; moving it to another compartment of the same container is this same call with the new `compartment`. Packing clears the item's own current location and holder; if someone currently holds the item, packing takes it from them — tell your user when that applies (the holder is visible on get_item). Both sides must be serialized items in this organization: quantity-tracked stock is not packed with this tool — its units go into a container from the item's stock section in the app (read them back as `packed` on get_item / check_item_availability); containers nest up to three levels (compartments are not a level); lost/retired items, items reserved for an active order (also a container that holds such an item, since packing moves its contents too) and containers switched to «cannot hold items» are rejected. Requires the manager role. Idempotent: re-packing into the same container and compartment changes nothing. Undo = unpack_item.

compartment.description: Compartment of the container, by name (case-insensitive) or id; null = directly in the container, outside any compartment. Omit to keep the current compartment (same container) or to put it directly in another container

containerId.description: Item id of the container to pack it into

name: pack_item

compartment.description: The compartment of that container the item sits in (absent = directly in the container)

container.description: The container this item is packed into, if any

effectiveHolder.description: Holder followed through the container chain

effectiveLocation.description: Location followed through the container chain

isDraft.description: Present and true only for an unfinished draft capture

modelId.description: The item's model — pass it as create_order lines[].modelId to order any instance of this model

primaryCode.description: The code printed on the item's asset tag — how a human tells two identical models apart. Absent when no code is attached

quantity.description: How many this row stands for — only on quantity-tracked pools. To count a pool, SUM this; to count serialized items, count rows

status.description: Condition: available | in_repair | defect | lost | retired ("available" means not defect/lost/retired — the item may still be borrowed)

trackingMode.description: "quantity" for a stock pool counted by amount. Absent = a serialized item, i.e. this row IS one physical thing

webUrl.description: Link to this item in the web app — give it to your user so they can look at the record themselves. Absent when the deployment has no public address configured

title: Pack item into container
